audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty text is generic EVEN 5.5/10 and the whole page treats Chronobreak as the thing that decides the lane. It does not decide the LANE — it decides the all-in.
audit.why: Ekko's laning weakness is that Phase Dive is a 325-range roll and Parallel Convergence needs him to walk into his own anomaly to get the stun and shield. Both are answerable by a held charm; that is why the content layer and the packet give Ahri levels 1-5.
audit.corrected: Difficulty re-grounded on Phase Dive's 325 range and the anomaly's entry condition, with Chronobreak moved to where it belongs — the commit, not the lane.
sources: brief.enemyKit W text ('If Ekko enters the anomaly, he gains shielding and stuns')

audit.whatIsWrong: Six level-chart rows disagree between layers. The full layer reads Skill on all seven; the content layer reads Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri/Skill/Ekko.
audit.why: The packet levelChart matches the content layer exactly. The full layer is a flat template that was never updated, so the page currently answers 'who wins Level 1' two different ways.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side -> Ahri, phases[6].side -> Ekko, phases[5] stays Skill. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] says Ekko survives lane 'using Timewinder's shield form as a getout tool'. Timewinder is his Q — a grenade that expands and rewinds. It grants no shield. The shield is on Parallel Convergence (W), and only when Ekko himself enters the anomaly.
audit.why: Riot's Q text describes damage, a slow field and a return hit, with no shield term anywhere. Riot's W text: 'If Ekko enters the anomaly, he gains shielding and stuns enemies by suspending them in time.' Putting the shield on the wrong ability sends the reader to watch the wrong cast.
audit.corrected: 'Survive lane using Parallel Convergence's shield and stun'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Charm stops Phase Dive, or that Chronobreak makes Ekko untargetable so charm and orb cannot touch him during it.
audit.why: Ahri's E 'instantly stops movement abilities'; Phase Dive is a 325-range roll into a blink to the target, so a held charm ends the engage before the blink resolves. Conversely Chronobreak's untargetable flag means every point of damage spent into the rewind is wasted — the missingInteractions entry flags exactly this.
audit.corrected: Charm-stops-Phase-Dive written into breakdown.carry and dosFull[0].d; the untargetable window written into winCon and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says 'count it out loud if you must' but never gives the count.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110/80/50 — it more than halves across its ranks. 'Commit on Chronobreak's cooldown' is sound advice at rank 1 and nearly meaningless at rank 3, and the page never distinguishes them.
audit.corrected: '110s at rank 1 but only 50s at rank 3, and he is untargetable through it. Save your last damage for the arrival.'

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing anywhere, despite Chronobreak healing for a percentage of damage received in the rewound window.
audit.why: Grievous Wounds applied before the rewind is what makes a won trade stay won. The missingInteractions entry flags needs-antiheal for exactly this reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood is the generic Ahri orb-trade line with no Ekko content.
audit.why: Timewinder hits twice — outbound and on the rewind back to Ekko. Standing off the return line is a concrete, matchup-specific way to halve his poke, and it is nowhere on the page.
sources: brief.enemyKit Q text ('the grenade rewinds back to Ekko, dealing damage on its return')

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES — 'Parallel Convergence' and 'Chronobreak' are Ekko's real W and R names and those lines were left alone. The genuine ability error was elsewhere and unflagged: wants.foe[1] attributed a shield to Timewinder (Q). Timewinder has no shield; Parallel Convergence (W) grants the shield, and only when Ekko himself enters the anomaly. Level chart: the full layer was flat 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and packet agreed on Ahri x5 / Skill / Ekko — six side flips proposed as one atomic group, with no matching win[] edits because win[] already reads correctly. Worth noting for a future pass: Parallel Convergence has a 1600-yard cast range, so Ekko can pre-place the anomaly from outside your Charm range (975) and outside your vision; nothing in either layer tells the reader that, and it is the main way the stun actually lands.
